items.question: How does bias-variance tradeoff affect model performance?
items.answer: The bias-variance tradeoff affects model performance by balancing the error caused by an overly complex model (bias) with the error caused by an underfitting model (variance). A good balance allows for accurate predictions, while an imbalance can lead to poor performance.

items.question: What is the difference between bagging and boosting in ensemble methods?
items.answer: Bagging and boosting are both ensemble methods used to improve model performance. Bagging creates multiple instances of a model on the same dataset, allowing each instance to make different predictions. Boosting, on the other hand, adds weights to individual predictions to produce a final prediction.

items.question: How do linear models differ from non-linear models?
items.answer: Linear models assume a linear relationship between inputs and outputs, whereas non-linear models can capture complex relationships. Linear models use equations like y = mx + b, while non-linear models use equations with higher degrees of freedom, such as polynomial or sigmoid functions.

items.question: Can you explain the concept of feature engineering in machine learning?
items.answer: Feature engineering involves selecting and transforming relevant input variables to improve model performance. This can include scaling, normalization, or encoding categorical variables, as well as creating new features that capture important relationships.

items.question: How do neural networks relate to deep learning?
items.answer: Neural networks are a type of machine learning algorithm that consists of layers of interconnected nodes (neurons). Deep learning extends this concept by stacking multiple layers of neurons, allowing for complex representations and improved performance on certain tasks.
